### 2026-10-10 – # Week 1 Journal: Building My Starbie PCB

**10h**

# Week 1 Journal: Building My Starbie PCB

Project: Starbie, a virtual pet on a custom PCB (XIAO ESP32-C3, OLED screen, MPU6050 motion sensor, DHT11 sensor, 2 buttons)
Tools: KiCad (Schematic Editor and PCB Editor)

## Goal for this session

Follow the Week 1 guide to design the PCB: draw the schematic, assign footprints, import the parts into the PCB editor, lay out the board, route it, check it for errors and export it.

## 1. Drawing the schematic

I added all the components in the Schematic Editor:

- **U2:** XIAO-ESP32-C3 microcontroller, with +5V, +3.3V and GND connected
- **SW1, SW2:** push buttons, one side on a net (GPIO2 / GPIO3) and the other side to GND
- **J1:** 4-pin header for the OLED screen (GND, 3.3V, SCL, SDA)
- **J2:** 8-pin header for the MPU6050 module (3.3V, GND, SCL, SDA)
- **U1:** DHT11 temperature and humidity sensor, with its data line on D1
- **R1:** 10K pull-up resistor from the DHT11 data line to 3.3V

![My finished schematic](PASTE-SCHEMATIC-SCREENSHOT-HERE)

## 2. Footprint assignment: where I got stuck

When I ran the footprint assignment tool and updated the PCB, **only J1 and U1 showed up on the board**.

![Error log from the first update](PASTE-FIRST-ERROR-LOG-SCREENSHOT-HERE)
![Only two parts imported into the PCB editor](PASTE-PCB-WITH-ONLY-J1-U1-SCREENSHOT-HERE)

The log said:

- `Cannot add J2, R1, SW1, SW2 (no footprint assigned)`
- `Cannot add U2 (footprint 'Seeed_Studio_XIAO_Series:XIAO-ESP32-C3-SMD' not found)`

### What I learned and fixed

1. **Missing footprints:** I had skipped J2, R1, SW1 and SW2 in the assignment tool. The XIAO was pointing to a library name my KiCad didn't have, so I reassigned it to the one in `StarbieFootprints` (from the care package).
2. **Wrong footprints:** I first assigned the OLED display footprint to everything, which gave errors like "pad 5, 6, 7, 8, MP not found". The correct picks were:
   - J2: `PinHeader_1x08_P2.54mm_Vertical`
   - R1: `R_Axial_DIN0204_L3.6mm_D1.6mm_P7.62mm_Horizontal`
   - SW1 and SW2: `SW_Cherry_MX_1.00u_PCB`
3. **Net labels not attached:** Several labels hadn't snapped to their wires, so pins landed on `unconnected` nets. I deleted the labels and replaced them with the **L** tool so the anchor sits exactly on the wire end. I also fixed a typo: one label read `GP102` (digit 1 and zero) instead of `GPIO2` (letter O).

![Footprint assignments, now correct](PASTE-FOOTPRINT-ASSIGNMENT-SCREENSHOT-HERE)

## 3. "Footprint is locked" errors

After fixing the assignments, the PCB update still failed:

> `Could not change J2 footprint ... (footprint is locked)`

The old wrong footprints were already on the board and locked, so KiCad wouldn't swap them. I fixed this by enabling **Locked items** in the Selection Filter, unlocking and deleting those four footprints, and pressing **F8** (Update PCB from Schematic) again.

## 4. The last error: the mounting pin

One error was left:

> `J2 pad MP not found in PinHeader_1x08_P2.54mm_Vertical`

J2's symbol was `Conn_01x08_MountingPin`, which has an extra MP pin that a plain pin header footprint doesn't have. Renaming the value didn't change the symbol. I used **Change Symbol** to switch it to `Connector_Generic:Conn_01x08`, then reassigned the J2 footprint, because changing the symbol cleared it.

**Result: 0 warnings, 0 errors.** The schematic and PCB are in sync.

![Clean update log with 0 errors](PASTE-CLEAN-LOG-SCREENSHOT-HERE)

## 5. PCB layout and board outline

All the footprints now imported into the PCB editor. I drew a **star-shaped outline** on the Edge.Cuts layer and arranged the parts inside it: the OLED (J1) in the centre, the MPU6050 header (J2) and the XIAO (U2) on the right, the two buttons on the left and bottom, and the DHT11 and resistor at the top.

I also learned that the outline can be any closed shape, and the star is just the guide's example.

![Components arranged inside the star outline](PASTE-LAYOUT-SCREENSHOT-HERE)

## 6. Routing the PCB

I routed the board by pressing **X**, clicking each pad that still had a thin blue ratsnest line, and drawing the trace to its partner pad. I worked on the **B.Cu** layer, used 45° corners for a cleaner look, and used vias (**V**) only where a trace had to cross another one. Power traces (+3.3V, +5V) are a bit wider than the signal traces. When I finished, no pad had a blue line left.

I also added a **GND copper pour** on the back layer. I drew a filled zone around the board, set its net to GND and pressed **B** to refill it. All the GND pads connected to it automatically.

![Routed PCB with GND pour](PASTE-ROUTED-PCB-SCREENSHOT-HERE)

## 7. Design rules check (DRC)

I ran **Inspect → Design Rules Checker**. As the guide predicted, the only errors left were the two it says to ignore, and there were no missing connections.

![DRC results](PASTE-DRC-SCREENSHOT-HERE)

## 8. Customization and export

I added some artwork to the board with the **Image Converter** tool, then exported the **Gerber files** and organised everything in my repository (schematic, PCB, footprints and Gerbers).

![Finished board in the 3D viewer](PASTE-3D-VIEW-SCREENSHOT-HERE)

## 9. Firmware

I set up the Arduino IDE, installed the ESP32 board package and the required libraries (Adafruit GFX, Adafruit SSD1306, Adafruit MPU6050 and DHT sensor library), selected the **XIAO_ESP32C3** board, and uploaded `Starbie.ino`.

## What I learned

- Footprints are what get drawn on the PCB, so every symbol needs the right one.
- A net label only connects if its anchor sits exactly on the wire end, and names must match exactly.
- The symbol and footprint must have matching pins (the MP pin problem).
- Locked footprints in the PCB block updates until they are unlocked.
- Reading the update log line by line shows exactly what is wrong.

## Checklist

- [x] Draw the schematic
- [x] Assign footprints
- [x] Import the parts into the PCB editor (0 errors)
- [x] Draw the board outline and arrange the parts
- [x] Finish routing all traces
- [x] Add a GND pour
- [x] Run DRC and fix errors
- [x] Add artwork with the Image Converter
- [x] Export Gerbers and organise the files in my repository
- [x] Upload the firmware with Arduino IDE
